note: Names and one-line summaries only (F0). impl is the proposed lowest kind that can do the job: deterministic < decision < llm.

capabilities.summary: Completes a task end to end as one general-purpose agent (T2 default) when no specialised capability fits.
Splits a request into a DAG of contracts linked by artifact types.
Writes one contract: goal, output schema, tools, boundaries, budget and deadline.
Produces a phase plan with milestones and exit criteria.
Summarises task and contract state from the ledger for a human reader.
Adds or updates risks with likelihood, impact, owner and mitigation.
Combines contract outputs into the final task result, including what is missing.
Decides whether a task is sequential or decomposable and how many independent branches it has.
Assigns value class A, B or C to a task from its description and type defaults.
Turns client material into a structured requirements specification.
Drafts a client proposal from requirements, scope and price.
Drafts a client e-mail; sending is a separate R3 action.
Extracts action items with owners and dates from client communication.
Decides whether a client request falls within the agreed scope.
Prepares a brief for a client meeting from earlier artifacts and decisions.
Writes an architecture decision record with options, decision and consequences.
Produces a system context diagram as diagram-as-code.
Compares technology options against stated criteria and recommends one.
Models an ArchiMate view for a given viewpoint and scope.
Specifies an API or integration interface with schemas and error cases.
Assesses a design against non-functional requirements such as performance and availability.
Reviews a design for gaps, risks and inconsistencies against requirements.
Decides whether a design contradicts an existing ADR or DECISION event.
Designs a data warehouse layer (staging, core, mart) with grain and keys.
Writes a lakehouse notebook that implements a specified transformation.
Defines a data contract: schema, semantics, quality rules and owner.
Generates metadata for a DWH-automation tool from a model design.
Reads schema metadata (tables, columns, keys) from a database without data access.
Computes column statistics, null rates and value distributions for a dataset.
Designs an ingestion pipeline with sources, schedule, load pattern and error handling.
Writes SQL for a specified transformation and its tests.
Maps source fields to a target model with transformation rules.
Checks a dataset against its data contract and reports violations.
Builds a KPI tree from business goals down to measurable indicators.
Writes a KPI definition: formula, grain, filters, owner and target.
Designs a star-schema semantic model and maps KPIs to measures.
Writes a measure expression for a defined KPI.
Runs a measure against test data and compares results with expected values.
Specifies a report: audience, pages, visuals, filters and measures.
Reviews a dashboard for clarity, correctness of visuals and KPI coverage.
Decides whether every required KPI is mapped to a measure in the design.
Implements a feature from a specification in an existing code base.
Finds the root cause of a reported bug and fixes it with a regression test.
Restructures code without changing behaviour, verified by existing tests.
Writes unit tests for specified behaviour, including edge cases.
Writes a deployment script with verification and rollback steps.
Writes a reversible database schema migration.
Writes a typed client for a documented API.
Upgrades a dependency and adapts code to breaking changes.
Explains a stack trace or error log and names the likely cause.
Writes a module overview: purpose, components and public API.
Runs a test suite in the sandbox and returns structured results.
Runs linters, type checks and formatters and returns findings.
Writes a prompt or skill for a capability contract.
Builds an eval set of 10 to 20 cases, including cases where abstention is correct.
Writes a single-judge rubric with scale and pass threshold.
Designs a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline: sources, chunking, index and retrieval.
Recommends a model and tier for a capability from eval results, cost and data policy.
Runs a capability's eval set and reports acceptance, abstention precision and cost.
Computes the autonomy threshold for a decision point from rated history.
Decides whether an agent is repeating itself without progress.
Reviews an output against its acceptance criteria and rubric with evidence.
Checks factual claims against cited sources and flags unsupported ones.
Designs test scenarios from requirements, including negative cases.
Decides whether one acceptance criterion is met by an output.
Decides whether an output states facts not supported by its inputs.
Decides whether a text contains instructions addressed to an agent.
Classifies a failed task by MAST category: specification, misalignment or verification.
Validates an artifact against its JSON Schema.
Builds a threat model with assets, threats, mitigations and residual risk.
Assesses a processing activity against GDPR requirements and lists gaps.
Proposes an EU AI Act risk classification for an AI system with reasoning.
Reviews granted permissions against least privilege and flags excess.
Decides the data class of an artifact: public, internal, client confidential, personal or special category.
Redacts detected personal and special-category entities from text.
Verifies that no detectable personal entity remains after redaction.
Extracts typed fields from invoices, receipts and statements.
Checks extracted invoice fields for completeness, totals and tax arithmetic.
Matches bank transactions to invoices by amount, reference and date.
Assigns a transaction to a category from a declared chart of accounts.
Reconciles account balances between two sources and lists differences.
Builds a cash-flow model with stated assumptions and scenarios.
Calculates unit economics (CAC, LTV, margin) from provided data and states assumptions.
Drafts an invoice from agreed work; issuing and sending are R3 actions.
Designs a landing-page funnel: sections, objections handled and calls to action.
Audits a page or site for SEO issues and prioritises fixes.
Writes marketing copy for a stated audience, channel and goal.
Profiles a competitor: offer, pricing, positioning and sources.
Plans a content calendar with topics, channels and dates.
Drafts a social media post; publishing is a separate R3 action.
Computes A/B test results with significance and confidence intervals.
Scores a lead against declared qualification criteria.
Researches a question on the web and returns findings with sources.
Looks up an entity in a public register through its API.
Scans papers on a topic and summarises findings with citations.
Compares vendors or products on declared criteria with sources.
Summarises one source document, keeping claims traceable to passages.
Rates a source's reliability on a declared scale.
Writes a technical document from artifacts for a stated audience.
Writes step-by-step user documentation for a feature.
Translates text while keeping terminology, format and placeholders.
Summarises a meeting transcript into decisions, action items and open questions.
Edits a text for clarity and length without changing its meaning.
